newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BankWest sees few opportunities in Asia.
newsitem.headline: BankWest sees few opportunities in Asia.

text.p: The Bank of Western Australia Ltd sees limited opportunities for expansion into Asia, managing director Warwick Kent said on Wednesday.
Responding to a shareholder's question at the bank's annual meeting in Perth, Kent said BankWest periodically conducts feasibility studies on expansion opportunities in Asia.
"There are very limited opportunities," he said.
"There are so many banks operating throughout Asia - local banks and other international banks.
"We are a small bank in the world - we have got to accept that," he said.
"We don't have the resources to put a huge investment into developing an infrastructure," Kent said.
BankWest operates a representative office in Singapore and attracts a large number of mainly Asian overseas students through branches on university campuses in Western Australia.
BankWest is owned 53 percent by Bank of Scotland.
Today's meeting passed all agenda items, including an employee incentive scheme and an executive share options scheme on a show of hands.
